Lead Leg Low Kick Basics for Southpaw

Southpaw is mostly rare because it is relegated to lefties, who are a lower percentage of the population - and some of those lefties are shoehorned into still using the orthodox stance. Few people intentionally buck the Righties-Orthodox/Lefties-Southpaw trend, but of those that do, righties fighting as Southpaw tends (or used to tend) to be rarer. Bruce Lee favored fighting with strong side forward, bucking the traditional thinking of boxing and (some) kickboxing orthodox stance strategy (Muay Thai from what I know is more receptive to Southpaw).

Thoughts?

I am retired now, but fought for years as a right handed person (write with right hand, throw with right hand) who fought southpaw. Most people fight orthodox, and I'm used to fighting left side forward (orthodox) people while most of those fight very few southpaw's, which served me very well.

For me, it was fairly easy to develop power in my off hand and foot, and was easy to develop speed and accuracy in my dominant side, and I was fortunate to have an instructor who was OK with this approach.

Awesome man!

Did you feel like the advantage was more from the strength of the strong side forward southpaw stance, or more from the surprise factor of throwing your opponent off?

I have mostly a TKD background so Im comfortable with kicking on both sides from both stances but Ive always sparred southpaw in that and relied heavily on lead leg stop-hits. Left rear punching power is the thing Im still working most to develop.

I think it was a combination of having strongest/fastest hand forward and having strongest fastest foot forward for front snap kicks, and side kicks, combined with the fact that I saw orthodox fighters all the time and southpaw was generally something the other guy saw only rarely.

For whatever reason, I can punch, and Thai kick (low) just as effectively with left as right, but many of my lead side techniques (especially kicks) I could only do with my right.
